finding: Both shell-level doors into Compare are offered while a review round is OPEN, and in that state the approved side cannot exist — so they land on an empty state whose sentence names a cause that is not the cause, and the four content boards are never reached.
evidence: ReviewBar renders only for round.status PENDING|CHANGES_REQUESTED (ReviewBar.tsx:50,116) and carries Compare (:144) wired to openLeftPanelToTab('review','compare') (AquibraStudio.tsx:535) -> ReviewTab initialCompare (:333-336) -> openCompare() -> fetchApprovedSnapshot(). ReviewTab's foot Compare (:411-420, mounted :833) is likewise ungated. getApprovedSnapshot queries status:'APPROVED', revokedAt:null (review.service.ts:370-374), and submitReview revokes every other tokened round when a new one opens (review.service.ts:105-108), so while a round is live the query returns null. ApprovedCompareView then renders 'No approved snapshot for this round / This review was sent before snapshots were captured' (:119-130) — a claim about snapshot capture, when the real cause is 'this round is not approved yet'. Contrast SavesChrome, which gates its Compare on isApproved (SavesChrome.tsx:112,117).
fix: Gate ReviewBar.tsx:144 and ReviewTab.tsx:411 on review state approved|approved-edited-since, the rule SavesChrome already applies; and split the null state's copy so 'no approved round yet' and 'approved round predates snapshot capture' are two different sentences (the transport collapses both to null today — review.service.ts:375-377).

finding: 168:2 is the destination of all three external doors into Compare and it is the only board in the family with no way out — every other live board carries a back chip, this one does not, and its frame-level click sends any click to Overlay instead.
evidence: Fetched 2026-09-05. Inbound to 168:2: node 633:4005 on 162:2 History · Saves; node 963:4758 on 963:4474 Shell · 360 overlay panel (inside a frame named 'overlay/History (360)'); node 881:4607 on 807:6965 Reference conflict board — all ON_CLICK->168:2. Outbound from 168:2: frame-level ON_CLICK->168:26, plus chips 1671:7285->168:48, 1672:7227->169:2, 444:2384->169:28, 444:2382->168:82. No destination 156:2 and no hotspot named back. 168:26/168:48/168:82/169:2 each carry 'hotspot/back · Review panel · open' (1671:7289/7293/7297/7301) at (150,738) 150x34.
fix: Add a back chip to 168:2 in the empty (0,706) slot, pointing at whichever board the user came from — see W-N-03 on which that should be.

finding: Compare's back always returns to the Review panel, but two of its three doors are History · Saves and a History overlay — so a user who opens Compare from their saves list is put down in a different panel and cannot get back to the list they left. The board and the code make the same one-way door.
evidence: All four back chips target 156:2 'Review panel · open' (1671:7289/7293/7297/7301, fetched 2026-09-05), while the inbound chips sit on 162:2 History · Saves (633:4005) and inside 'overlay/History (360)' on 963:4474 (963:4758). Code: SavesChrome's 'Compare with current' emits UI_PANEL_OPEN {panel:'review',screen:'compare'} (SavesChrome.tsx:133-138), useEditorEventListeners.ts:151-155 routes it, openLeftPanelToTab switches the left tab to review (useStudioState.ts:317-327), and leaving Compare is setCompareOpen(false) (ReviewTab.tsx:501) which lands on the Review panel's own list. The History tab is gone by then.
fix: Carry the opener through the deep link and make Compare's exit return to it; the chip on 168:2 (W-N-02) should point at 162:2, not 156:2.

screen: Compare · entered from the Review panel
finding: The Review panel's own Compare route never reaches this section: it dead-ends in two orphan 280px fragments that only link to each other, so the success branch of the panel's Compare button has no board at any width. Corroborates D-D-10 with a second, independent read.
evidence: Fetched page-wide reaction scan 2026-09-05 returned six inbound edges to Compare boards, from 162:2, 963:4474 and 807:6965 only — zero from any 15x Review board. The Review compare pair sits outside the section: 1717:17246 'Review · compare · loading' 280x260 -> 156:2 and 1717:17235 'Review · compare · load-error' 280x300 -> 1717:17246 (baselines/figma-page-1-3-pre-reorg.tsv:812-813). Code takes the Review route for every entry — ReviewTab.tsx:497-531 is the only mount of ApprovedCompareView.
fix: Either wire 156:2's compare hotspot to 168:2 and retire the two fragments, or adopt them as the family's drawer-width states and build the missing success board beside them (see W-N-22).

screen: Compare · all states, at the width they ship
finding: Compare is drawn at 1080 and ships inside the 280px left drawer, and the one control that could widen it is the one the compare screen removes — so a user cannot get more room for a side-by-side without first leaving Compare.
evidence: All eight members are 1080x776 (fetched section listing, 2026-09-05). Shipping width: tokens.generated.css:129 --bk-size-drawer: 280px, consumed at LeftSidebar.css:231. The expand toggle sets 700 (LeftSidebar.tsx:580-589) and reaches panels via PanelHeader's isExpanded/onExpandToggle (PanelHeader.tsx:115,153-154), but ReviewTab's compare branch renders a bare Toolbar with a Back button and no {header} (ReviewTab.tsx:497-531), so no expand control exists inside Compare. openLeftPanelToTab does not set expanded either (useStudioState.ts:317-327). Recorded drift: jobs.json J-168:2 'drift-compare-in-320-drawer-not-1080-surface'.
fix: Either render PanelHeader inside the compare branch so expand survives, or open Compare through an overlay at the drawn width (the shell board 963:4474 already draws a 360 overlay slot for it).

finding: While the current side is still rendering, the change count and the List body are computed against an empty site — so every page reads 'removed since approval'. Reading board 169:28 against the code found it: the board asserts a change count in a state where none can be known, and the code invents one.
evidence: ApprovedCompareView computes result = compareApprovedToCurrent(approvedPages, currentPages ?? []) unconditionally (:113-116); with currentPages null every approved path takes the a && !c branch and emits kind 'removed', label `Page ${path}` (approvedCompare.ts:244-246). The nothingChanged guard is gated on currentReady (:132,140) but the count span (:165-168) and the List body (:194-227) are not. ReviewTab sets currentPages to null on every open (:313) and ApprovedCompareView is mounted as soon as the APPROVED read resolves (:506-517), so this state is reached on every Compare. Board 169:28 (screenshot, fetched 2026-09-05) prints '12 changes · 3 of 12' over a right pane reading 'rendering…'.
fix: Gate the count and the List body on currentReady, the same way nothingChanged already is; show the count as '—' or suppress it until the current side arrives. Board side: drop or neutralise 169:39's count.

finding: The close control drawn in the top-right of every Compare board is dead on all six, and on the entry board it is worse than dead — the board-level click takes it to Overlay.
evidence: Fetched geometry 2026-09-05: 168:14, 168:38, 168:60, 168:94, 169:14, 169:40 are all TEXT '✕' at (1052,14) 12x20 inside 'Compare bar', every one with zero reactions. Every hotspot on these boards is a 150x34 prototype chip parked at the foot (y=706/738/742), 700+px away, so none covers the ✕. On 168:2 the frame itself carries ON_CLICK->168:26, so a click on the ✕ opens Overlay. This is the only exit affordance drawn anywhere in the family — no board draws a '‹ Back'.
fix: Give the ✕ its own reaction on each board (168:2 -> its opener per W-N-03, the rest -> the same), or replace it with a back affordance so it matches what the code renders (ReviewTab.tsx:500-505 draws '‹ Back' and no close).

screen: Compare · side-by-side / overlay / list / no-changes / loading-render
finding: 'Home ▾' — the page switcher, the only way to move between pages in a multi-page compare — has no reaction on any board and no open-dropdown state is drawn anywhere in the section.
evidence: 168:12, 168:36, 168:58, 168:92, 169:38 are TEXT 'Home  ▾' in the Compare bar, no reactions (fetched trees + geometry, 2026-09-05). The section's 16 members are 8 boards + 8 captions; none is a picker. The control is real in code — ApprovedCompareView.tsx:169-179 renders a Select of page paths whenever paths.length > 1. 169:2 correctly omits it and says why in its note (169:27), which proves the omission elsewhere is not intentional.
fix: Draw the open picker as a state off 168:2 and wire 'Home ▾' to it. See W-N-14 for what it can actually list.

finding: The mode strip is only fully wired on two of five boards. From List you cannot reach Overlay; from no-changes and single-page you cannot reach either of the other two — the segments are drawn, and clicking them either does nothing or jumps to Side-by-side.
evidence: Fetched 2026-09-05. 168:2: frame->168:26 (Overlay) + chip 1671:7285->168:48 (List) — complete. 168:26: frame->168:48 + chip 1671:7287->168:2 — complete. 168:48: frame->168:2 only, no Overlay hotspot. 168:82: frame->168:2 only. 169:2: no frame-level reaction at all; its only chips are 1671:7299 (side-by-side) and 1671:7301 (back), so seg/Overlay (169:8) and seg/List (169:10) do nothing. The census could not have caught these: the frame-level reaction on 168:2/168:26/168:48/168:82/169:28 marks every descendant 'wired' by its ancestor test (dead-control-census.mjs, the `wired` flag propagated down the stack).
fix: Add the missing mode chips so all three segments resolve from every mode board, or move the mode strip into a component instance whose segments carry the reactions once.

finding: A leftover prototype chip sits in the entry board's navigation strip with its reaction removed — a 150x34 target in a row of live ones that answers nothing.
evidence: 444:2386 'hotspot/state · Compare · resend-confirm — C[name truncated at 44 chars by the read]' FRAME at (300,742) 150x34, zero reactions (fetched 2026-09-05), sitting in the same row as 444:2382 (0,742 -> 168:82) and 444:2384 (150,742 -> 169:28). Its reaction was cut on 2026-09-02 when 169:92 was superseded (LEDGER.jsonl, coordinator-figma job C2), but the node was left behind.
fix: Delete node 444:2386.

finding: Three candidates dismissed as FINE, recorded so the split is auditable: the change counter, the mode strip's selected-state treatment, and the note blocks.
evidence: 168:13/168:37/168:59/168:93/169:13/169:39 '12 changes · 3 of 12' reads like a stepper but is a label — the code prints the identical string (ApprovedCompareView.tsx:165-168), no prev/next exists on either side. The mode strip's convention is consistent across all six boards (screenshots 168-2/168-26/168-48): the grey track holds the UNSELECTED segments and the selected one sits outside it, merging when unselected segments are adjacent — unusual but legible, not a defect. 168:46/169:26/169:58 'note' frames are designer annotations per the coordinator ruling of 2026-09-03 (LEDGER.jsonl, J-164:22) and are not UI.
fix: No change. One caveat: on 168:82 the same kind of sentence (168:97, 'No panes render — an empty diff view reads as broken.') is a direct child of Body rather than a note frame, so it renders as body copy under the headline — see the screenshot. Move it into a note frame like its siblings.

finding: Every board labels the left pane 'v3 · approved'. Nothing in the code knows a version number or an approval date at this point, so the field has no home and the pane can only say 'Approved'.
evidence: Board TEXT 168:17, 169:17, 169:43 = 'v3 · approved' (fetched 2026-09-05, seen in screenshots 168-2 / 169-28). getApprovedSnapshot returns {path, html}[] and nothing else (review.service.ts:353-377); the ReviewRequest select is `{ snapshotPages: true }` (:373). ApprovedCompareView's props are approvedPages/currentPages/onRefreshCurrent (:39-45) and it labels the pane 'Approved' (:264). ReviewTab.tsx:26-27 records the same conclusion for the button label: "Compare is labelled 'Compare with approved' rather than the board's 'Compare with v3' (nothing here knows a version number)".
fix: Either drop the version clause from the boards, or widen the approvedSnapshot payload to carry the round's number and resolvedAt — a shared-schema change, not a board fix.

finding: The boards name pages the way a user does ('Home'); the shipped picker lists export filenames ('index.html'), and page-level change rows print 'Page index.html'. No page title reaches Compare at all.
evidence: ComparePage is {path, html} (approvedCompare.ts:49-52) and PublishPage the same (exportPublishPages.ts:6-9). exportPublishPages maps path = f.name (:28-35) and ExportEngine writes fileName = this.pageHrefs.get(page.id) ?? 'index.html' (ExportEngine.ts:716). The Select renders <option>{p}</option> over those paths (ApprovedCompareView.tsx:175-177). Page-level changes are labelled `Page ${path}` (approvedCompare.ts:245,247), so a removed home page reads 'Page index.html — Page removed since approval'.
fix: Carry the page name alongside the path in the compare payload (Composer knows it at export time), or accept filenames and change the boards to draw them.

finding: The shipped Overlay is an opacity blend driven by a slider, and no board draws the slider or its two end labels. 168:26 draws a single annotated pane instead — it is not an overlay of two versions at all.
evidence: Board 168:26 (screenshot + tree, fetched 2026-09-05) is one pane titled 'Current, with changes marked' (168:41) holding a blue 'changed' block (168:43) and a yellow 'deleted — “Happy hour, 5–7pm”' strip (168:45). No slider node, no 'Approved'/'Current' labels. Code: two stacked sandboxed iframes with the current one at overlayOpacity (ApprovedCompareView.tsx:229-244) plus a Toolbar carrying 'Approved' — Slider(label 'Overlay opacity', 0-100, step 2) — 'Current' (:245-259). Already recorded as drift-overlay-is-opacity-blend-not-highlights (jobs.json J-168:26); the half nobody has noted is that the CONTROL has no board.
fix: Redraw 168:26 as the blend with its slider, or board the slider separately if the tint direction is being kept as design-ahead.

finding: The code emits five change kinds with an icon, a kind label, a detail line, a per-kind summary and a five-item legend; the list board draws three verbs, a colour dot, no legend and no summary. 'moved' has no representation anywhere in the file.
evidence: Code kinds content|style|added|removed|moved (approvedCompare.ts:28), each with icon + className + label (ApprovedCompareView.tsx:49-57), a summary line '3 content · 2 style' (:198-202) and a five-item legend (:280-293) — the header comment ties this to design codex #6, colour never the sole encoding. Board 168:48 rows (fetched tree + screenshot): ELLIPSE + label + verb, verbs 'edited' x3, '2 images added', 'deleted' (168:62-168:81). No legend frame, no summary frame on 168:48 or on 168:2/168:26. 'moved' is produced at approvedCompare.ts:207 and drawn nowhere.
fix: Redraw the list row as icon + kind label + detail, add the summary line and the legend, and add a 'moved' example — otherwise building to this board removes the non-colour encoding (already the recorded reason 168:48 was skipped, LEDGER 2026-09-03).

finding: The 'Re-render the current site' control that ships in the Compare bar is on no board.
evidence: ApprovedCompareView.tsx:180-184 renders a RefreshCw button, title/aria-label 'Re-render the current site', wired to onRefreshCurrent, which ReviewTab supplies (:518-527). The Compare bar on every board is exactly: 'Compare' title, mode strip, 'Home ▾', count, '✕' (fetched trees for all six live boards, 2026-09-05). No refresh node.
fix: Add it to the bar on 168:2 and the states that inherit the bar, or decide the control is not wanted and remove it from the code.

finding: Two boards print a change count their own body contradicts: the no-changes board says '12 changes · 3 of 12' above 'Nothing changed since v3.', and the still-loading board asserts 12 changes before the current side exists.
evidence: 168:93 and 169:39 both read '12 changes · 3 of 12' (fetched trees; seen in screenshots 168-82 and 169-28). The code is right on the first: nothingChanged replaces the body and result.changes.length is 0, so the span reads '0 changes' (ApprovedCompareView.tsx:140,165-168). It is wrong on the second — see W-N-06.
fix: Set 168:93 to '0 changes' and neutralise 169:39, so a builder conforming to the bar does not print a false count.

finding: Not one of the six live Compare states is drawn at the width Compare actually ships at, so nothing in this section is buildable as drawn — the family is eight 1080px boards for a surface that renders in a 280px drawer.
evidence: Section members are all 1080x776 (fetched listing 2026-09-05). Shipping surface: ApprovedCompareView is mounted only at ReviewTab.tsx:517, inside the left drawer, whose width is --bk-size-drawer: 280px (tokens.generated.css:129, LeftSidebar.css:231), expandable to 700 but not from inside Compare (W-N-05). Two side-by-side iframes at 280 leaves ~135px per pane. The only drawer-width compare art in the file is the orphan pair 1717:17246 / 1717:17235 (280x260 / 280x300), which draw loading and error and no result. A third width is implied by 963:4474, whose compare chip sits in a frame named 'overlay/History (360)'.
fix: Decide the surface first — 280 drawer, 360 overlay, or a 1080 overlay opened via OverlayMount — then redraw the six states at it. Side-by-side is the mode that decides the answer; List survives any width.

finding: The state Compare reaches most often has no board: 'No approved snapshot for this round'. It is a different fact from no-changes, and per W-N-01 it is where both shell-level doors always land.
evidence: ApprovedCompareView.tsx:119-130 returns an EmptyState (History icon, 'No approved snapshot for this round', 'This review was sent before snapshots were captured…') that replaces the entire body, before the toolbar is even rendered — so no mode strip, no count, no page picker. Reached whenever getApprovedSnapshot returns null: no APPROVED round, an approval revoked by a later submit (review.service.ts:105-108,370-374), a snapshot pruned as superseded (:134-145), or agency_layer off (reviews.ts:185). There is a covering test — ApprovedCompareView.test.tsx:37 'shows an explicit state when the round has no snapshot' — and no board.
fix: Draw it from 168:82: same empty-body shape, different headline, and the bar suppressed rather than printed (168:82 keeps a bar this state has no data for). Split the copy per W-N-01.

screen: Compare · after comparing, nothing to do
finding: Compare is read-only and the code agrees — and the two boards that once gave it an action were both removed on the same day rather than built, so 'decide whether to keep or discard a change' now has no surface at all.
evidence: ApprovedCompareView's complete control set is three mode buttons, a count span, a page Select and a refresh button (:148-185) — no restore, no accept, no discard, no re-send, no approve. ReviewTab's compare screen adds only '‹ Back' and drops the PanelHeader entirely (:497-531), so there is no close, no expand and no primary either. 169:60 'Compare · restore-confirm' was RETIRED 2026-09-02 (no producer) and 169:92 'Compare · resend-confirm' SUPERSEDED by 158:2, both with their inbound hotspots cut (LEDGER.jsonl, coordinator-figma job C2; the leftover chip is W-N-10). Their outbound reactions survive but nothing reaches them: 169:60->163:220, 169:92->158:57. Every action a user might want after comparing lives in a different panel they must navigate back to — and per W-N-03 back goes to the wrong one.
fix: Decide whether Compare is a viewer or a decision surface. If a viewer, say so in the family's caption and make the exit return to the panel that owns the action (History for restore, Review for re-send). If a decision surface, 169:60's copy is already written and correct ('Restore v3 and lose 12 changes? Your current work is saved as v4 first') and needs a producer — restore-to-approved needs a ProjectData snapshot captured at reviews.submit, not the HTML snapshotPages the compare reads.

finding: The compare screen's own failure state — 'Couldn't load the approved snapshot' with a Retry — has no board in this section; the only art for it is a 280x300 orphan that links to nothing in the family.
evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:508-515 renders EmptyState(AlertCircle, "Couldn't load the approved snapshot", "The dashboard didn't answer. Try again.", action=Retry->openCompare). Reached whenever fetchApprovedSnapshot throws (:323-325) — the DF5 rule that a transport failure must never render as a fake 'nothing changed'. The section's eight members contain no error state (fetched listing 2026-09-05). 1717:17235 'Review · compare · load-error' 280x300 exists outside the section and its only edge is back to 1717:17246 (baselines/figma-page-1-3-pre-reorg.tsv:812).
fix: Draw it from 168:82 at whatever width W-N-18 settles, and fold 1717:17235 into the family or retire it.

screen: Compare · page present on one side only
finding: A page added or deleted since approval renders one live pane and one 'Not present on this side' placeholder — a state the comparator explicitly produces and no board draws.
evidence: Frame() returns the placeholder whenever the page is absent from that side (ApprovedCompareView.tsx:88-93). compareApprovedToCurrent emits kind 'added'/'removed' at page level for exactly this (approvedCompare.ts:244-247), and the page union that feeds the picker includes both sides (ApprovedCompareView.tsx:103-108), so the missing-side page is selectable. Both overlay and split hit it (:233,238,265,270). No board in the section draws a half-empty diptych — 168:2, 169:2 and 169:28 all draw two populated panes (screenshots, fetched 2026-09-05).
fix: Add it as a state off 168:2, and decide what the Overlay mode does when one side has nothing to blend.

finding: A whole third compare surface shipped in September with no board anywhere in the file — the one that answers 'what changed between two published versions', which is half the job this section is named for.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/PublishDiffView.tsx, 103 lines, four states: loading skeleton (:59), error + Try again (:61-68), 'one of these versions is older than the kept window' (:70-77), and the per-page result list with added/removed/changed/unchanged badges and KB deltas (:79-100). Entered from a per-row Compare button on every published version but the oldest (PublishHistory.tsx:317-324, mounted :292). Landed 2026-09-04 per jobs.json F-COMPARE-NO-DIFF. The nearest board, 807:8787, is named '[not-implemented] S6.3 · publish-changelog · diff-summary', is 1440x900 and hangs off the Publish panel, not History · Published — its not-implemented marker is now stale.
fix: Board the four states from 168:48 (the list row is the same shape: identity, kind, detail) at the width History · Published actually renders, and re-mark 807:8787.

finding: The publish diff has no zero-change state, so a redeploy with no content change prints '0 changed · 0 added · 0 removed · N unchanged' over N Unchanged rows — the exact failure 168:82's own annotation was written to prevent.
evidence: PublishDiffView.tsx:81-98 renders the summary and the full page list unconditionally when diff.retained is true; 'same' is a first-class badge (:30). Board 168:82's annotation (168:97): 'No panes render — an empty diff view reads as broken.' ApprovedCompareView honours that rule (:140,187-193) and PublishDiffView does not.
fix: Apply 168:82's rule to the publish diff: replace the body when changed+added+removed is 0.

finding: 'See what changed between two versions' only works for adjacent pairs — the Compare button always diffs a row against the one below it, and no picker for an arbitrary pair exists in code or on any board.
evidence: PublishHistory.tsx:319 hardcodes from = rows[i+1], to = r, and the button is omitted on the last row (:317 `i < rows.length - 1`). PublishDiffViewProps takes explicit from/to (:19-24), so the service supports any pair — fetchPublishDiff(siteId, from.id, to.id) (:43) — and only the UI narrows it.
fix: Add a from/to selector to the diff header; the board can reuse the 'Home ▾' picker pattern once W-N-08 gives it an open state.
